claim: RpaA is the master regulator of circadian transcription in cyanobacteria
source: The transcription factor RpaA is the master regulator of circadian transcription in cyanobacteria, driving genome-wide oscillations in mRNA abundance.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations to prior work throughout the manuscript.

claim: RpaA drives genome-wide oscillations in mRNA abundance
source: The transcription factor RpaA is the master regulator of circadian transcription in cyanobacteria, driving genome-wide oscillations in mRNA abundance.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by references to prior studies.

claim: Deletion of rpaA has no effect on viability in constant light conditions
source: Deletion of rpaA has no effect on viability in constant light conditions, but renders cells inviable in cycling conditions when light and dark periods alternate.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1A.

claim: Deletion of rpaA renders cells inviable in cycling conditions when light and dark periods alternate
source: Deletion of rpaA has no effect on viability in constant light conditions, but renders cells inviable in cycling conditions when light and dark periods alternate.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The rpaA- strain cannot maintain appropriate energy status at night
source: We investigated the mechanisms underlying this viability defect, and demonstrate that the rpaA- strain cannot maintain appropriate energy status at night, does not accumulate carbon reserves during the day, and is defective in transcription of genes crucial for utilization of carbohydrate stores at night.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by energy charge measurements in Figure 2.

claim: The rpaA- strain does not accumulate carbon reserves during the day
source: We investigated the mechanisms underlying this viability defect, and demonstrate that the rpaA- strain cannot maintain appropriate energy status at night, does not accumulate carbon reserves during the day, and is defective in transcription of genes crucial for utilization of carbohydrate stores at night.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by glycogen measurements in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: The rpaA- strain is defective in transcription of genes crucial for utilization of carbohydrate stores at night
source: We investigated the mechanisms underlying this viability defect, and demonstrate that the rpaA- strain cannot maintain appropriate energy status at night, does not accumulate carbon reserves during the day, and is defective in transcription of genes crucial for utilization of carbohydrate stores at night.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by RNA-seq data in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Reconstruction of carbon utilization pathways combined with provision of an external carbon source restores energy charge and viability of the rpaA- strain in light/dark cycling conditions
source: Reconstruction of carbon utilization pathways combined with provision of an external carbon source restores energy charge and viability of the rpaA- strain in light/dark cycling conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in Figure 5A, 5B, and 5D.

claim: The circadian output pathway controls and temporally coordinates essential pathways in carbon metabolism to maximize fitness of cells facing periodic energy limitations
source: Our observations highlight how a circadian output pathway controls and temporally coordinates essential pathways in carbon metabolism to maximize fitness of cells facing periodic energy limitations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The core circadian oscillator in Synechococcus elongatus PCC7942 is comprised of the KaiA, KaiB and KaiC proteins
source: In the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC7942, the core circadian oscillator is comprised of the KaiA, KaiB and KaiC proteins (Nishiwaki et al., 2007; Rust et al., 2007) that generate oscillations in the phosphorylation state of KaiC.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: The KaiABC proteins generate oscillations in the phosphorylation state of KaiC
source: In the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC7942, the core circadian oscillator is comprised of the KaiA, KaiB and KaiC proteins (Nishiwaki et al., 2007; Rust et al., 2007) that generate oscillations in the phosphorylation state of KaiC.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Time information encoded in the phosphorylation state of KaiC is transmitted to the transcription factor RpaA
source: Time information encoded in the phosphorylation state of KaiC is transmitted to the transcription factor RpaA (Takai et al., 2006; Taniguchi et al., 2010; Markson et al., 2013) to generate circadian changes in gene expression (Markson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: More than 60% of protein-coding genes in S. elongatus are regulated in a circadian manner in continuous light
source: In continuous light, the expression of more than 60% of protein-coding genes in S. elongatus is regulated in a circadian manner (Vijayan et al., 2009) with two main phases of gene expression: genes peaking at subjective dawn or subjective dusk, where the term 'subjective' refers to an internal estimate of time in the absence of external cues.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Circadian gene expression in S. elongatus has two main phases: genes peaking at subjective dawn or subjective dusk
source: In continuous light, the expression of more than 60% of protein-coding genes in S. elongatus is regulated in a circadian manner (Vijayan et al., 2009) with two main phases of gene expression: genes peaking at subjective dawn or subjective dusk, where the term 'subjective' refers to an internal estimate of time in the absence of external cues.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Deletion of rpaA disrupts rhythms in mRNA abundance and arrests cells in a subjective dawn-like transcriptional state
source: Deletion of rpaA disrupts these rhythms in mRNA abundance and arrests cells in a subjective dawn-like transcriptional state, rendering them unable to switch to a subjective dusk-like expression program (Markson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The rpaA- strain is unable to switch to a subjective dusk-like expression program
source: Deletion of rpaA disrupts these rhythms in mRNA abundance and arrests cells in a subjective dawn-like transcriptional state, rendering them unable to switch to a subjective dusk-like expression program (Markson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: Wild type and the rpaA- cells grow at the same rate in constant light
source: As reported previously (Takai et al., 2006), in constant light wild type and the rpaA- cells grow at the same rate (Figure 1A, top panel)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1A and a citation to prior work.

claim: The rpaA- strain rapidly loses viability when incubated in the dark
source: The rpaA- strain rapidly loses viability when incubated in the dark (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the defect is induced by darkness and not by repeated light-to-dark and dark-to-light transitions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The viability defect in the rpaA- strain is induced by darkness and not by repeated light-to-dark and dark-to-light transitions
source: The rpaA- strain rapidly loses viability when incubated in the dark (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the defect is induced by darkness and not by repeated light-to-dark and dark-to-light transitions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that cells lose viability in continuous darkness.

claim: Complementation of the rpaA- strain with rpaA expressed from an ectopic site in the genome fully restores viability
source: Complementation of the rpaA- strain with rpaA expressed from an ectopic site in the genome fully restores viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: Deletion of rpaA abrogates the function of the KaiABC oscillator
source: In wild type cells, expression of the kaiBC genes depends on RpaA and thus deletion of rpaA abrogates the function of the KaiABC oscillator, altering the stoichiometry of the core clock proteins and abrogating the rhythms in KaiC phosphorylation (Takai et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The viability defect during dark periods results from loss of RpaA function and not from loss of Kai oscillator function
source: We observed that the rpaA- 'clock rescue' strain phenocopies the rpaA- strain and the isogenic rpaA+ 'clock rescue' strain phenocopies wild type strain, demonstrating that the viability defect stems from the loss of RpaA function and not from loss of Kai oscillator function (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated by experiments using the 'clock rescue' strain background.

claim: Phosphorylation of RpaA is required for binding to its target promoters and gene expression
source: Since phosphorylation of RpaA is required for binding to its target promoters and gene expression (Markson et al., 2013), we asked whether the rpaA deletion phenotype in light/dark conditions can be rescued by a specific phosphorylated form of RpaA
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Expression of the RpaA D53E phosphomimetic restores viability in light/dark conditions
source: We observed that expression of the RpaA D53E phosphomimetic restores viability in light/dark conditions, while expression of the RpaA D53A variant does not (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of the RpaA D53A variant does not restore viability in light/dark conditions
source: We observed that expression of the RpaA D53E phosphomimetic restores viability in light/dark conditions, while expression of the RpaA D53A variant does not (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The active DNA-binding form of RpaA is necessary and sufficient for cell viability during exposure to light/dark conditions
source: We conclude that the active DNA-binding form of RpaA is necessary and sufficient for cell viability during exposure to light/dark conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phosphomimetic experiments.

claim: Deletion of the kaiBC operon leads to only a minor viability defect in light/dark conditions
source: Deletion of the kaiBC operon leads to only a minor viability defect in light/dark conditions (Boyd et al., 2013 and Figure 1D)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1D and a citation to prior work.

claim: RpaA remains highly phosphorylated throughout the light/dark cycle in the kaiBC- strain
source: In agreement with this prediction, when we analyzed RpaA phosphorylation in the kaiBC- mutant we detected high levels of RpaA phosphorylation both in light and in the dark (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1E.

claim: The ability of the kaiBC- mutant to survive alternating periods of light and dark likely stems from the high levels of phosphorylated RpaA in this strain
source: Thus, the ability of the kaiBC- mutant to survive alternating periods of light and dark likely stems from the high levels of phosphorylated RpaA in this strain.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that the kaiBC- mutant maintains high RpaA phosphorylation and survives light/dark cycles.

claim: The cKaiC-AA mutant is viable in light/dark conditions
source: We observed that while the cKaiC-AA mutant is viable in light/dark conditions, the cKaiC-EE strain is not able to grow (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1F.

claim: The cKaiC-EE strain is not able to grow in light/dark conditions
source: We observed that while the cKaiC-AA mutant is viable in light/dark conditions, the cKaiC-EE strain is not able to grow (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1F.

claim: The cKaiC-AA strain maintains high RpaA phosphorylation levels during the diurnal cycle
source: Strikingly, the cKaiC-AA strain maintains high RpaA phosphorylation levels during the diurnal cycle, while RpaA is phosphorylated in the cKaiC-EE strain only at a low level (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1G.

claim: RpaA is phosphorylated in the cKaiC-EE strain only at a low level
source: Strikingly, the cKaiC-AA strain maintains high RpaA phosphorylation levels during the diurnal cycle, while RpaA is phosphorylated in the cKaiC-EE strain only at a low level (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 1G.

claim: In constant light, there is no difference in energy charge between wild type and the rpaA- strain
source: In constant light, there was no difference in energy charge between wild type and the rpaA- strain (Figure 2, top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: Wild type cells subjected to darkness experience only a slight reduction in energy charge
source: Wild type cells subjected to darkness experience only a slight reduction in energy charge (Figure 2, bottom panel, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: rpaA- cells experience a reduction in energy charge during the first dark period and an even more dramatic reduction during the second dark period
source: In contrast, rpaA- cells experience a reduction in energy charge during the first dark period and an even more dramatic reduction during the second dark period, suggesting that this strain has a defect in energy metabolism affecting energy maintenance during the dark phase of the light/dark cycle (Figure 2, bottom panel, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: The rpaA- strain has a defect in energy metabolism affecting energy maintenance during the dark phase of the light/dark cycle
source: In contrast, rpaA- cells experience a reduction in energy charge during the first dark period and an even more dramatic reduction during the second dark period, suggesting that this strain has a defect in energy metabolism affecting energy maintenance during the dark phase of the light/dark cycle (Figure 2, bottom panel, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the energy charge measurements.

claim: The decrease in energy charge in the rpaA- strain is accompanied by a reduction in the total adenine nucleotide pool size
source: The decrease in energy charge was accompanied by a reduction in the total adenine nucleotide pool size in the rpaA- strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Genes relevant for carbon catabolism peak in mRNA abundance at subjective dusk in constant light conditions
source: In constant light conditions, the circadian program directs expression of anabolic and catabolic pathways, with genes relevant for carbon catabolism peaking in mRNA abundance at subjective dusk (Vijayan et al., 2009; Diamond et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior work.

claim: Expression of circadian dusk-peaking genes is most affected in the rpaA deletion strain exposed to darkness
source: The expression of circadian dusk-peaking genes was most affected in the rpaA deletion strain exposed to darkness (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Genes encoding enzymes involved in glycogen breakdown, glycolysis and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway are among the genes with the greatest defect in expression in the rpaA- cells
source: Specifically, we observed that genes encoding enzymes involved in glycogen breakdown, glycolysis and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary file 1), which normally peak in expression at dusk, are among the genes with the greatest defect in expression in the rpaA- cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Glycogen breakdown, glycolysis and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway are key for carbon utilization and energy production in the dark in cyanobacteria
source: These pathways are key for carbon utilization and energy production in the dark in cyanobacteria (Figure 3B), and their function is essential for survival of periods of darkness (Doolittle and Singer, 1974).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work and illustrated in Figure 3B.

claim: Independent deletion of gnd results in impaired viability in light/dark cycles but not in constant light conditions
source: Independent deletion of gnd as well as the glgP_gap1 and fbp_zwf_opcA operons, which exhibit severely reduced expression in the rpaA- strain, results in impaired viability in light/dark cycles but not in constant light conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Doolittle and Singer, 1974; Scanlan et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C with citations to prior work.

claim: Independent deletion of the glgP_gap1 operon results in impaired viability in light/dark cycles but not in constant light conditions
source: Independent deletion of gnd as well as the glgP_gap1 and fbp_zwf_opcA operons, which exhibit severely reduced expression in the rpaA- strain, results in impaired viability in light/dark cycles but not in constant light conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Doolittle and Singer, 1974; Scanlan et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C with citations to prior work.

claim: Independent deletion of the fbp_zwf_opcA operon results in impaired viability in light/dark cycles but not in constant light conditions
source: Independent deletion of gnd as well as the glgP_gap1 and fbp_zwf_opcA operons, which exhibit severely reduced expression in the rpaA- strain, results in impaired viability in light/dark cycles but not in constant light conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Doolittle and Singer, 1974; Scanlan et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C with citations to prior work.

claim: Activity of glycogen phosphorylase is strongly reduced in the rpaA- strain compared to wild type in the dark
source: To confirm that the transcriptional defects in the rpaA deletion mutant affect carbon catabolism, we measured the enzymatic activities of glycogen phosphorylase (glgP), glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (zwf) and 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (gnd) in the dark, and observed that activity of each enzyme was strongly reduced in the rpaA- strain compared to wild type (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3C.

claim: Activity of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase is strongly reduced in the rpaA- strain compared to wild type in the dark
source: To confirm that the transcriptional defects in the rpaA deletion mutant affect carbon catabolism, we measured the enzymatic activities of glycogen phosphorylase (glgP), glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (zwf) and 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (gnd) in the dark, and observed that activity of each enzyme was strongly reduced in the rpaA- strain compared to wild type (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3C.

claim: Activity of 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase is strongly reduced in the rpaA- strain compared to wild type in the dark
source: To confirm that the transcriptional defects in the rpaA deletion mutant affect carbon catabolism, we measured the enzymatic activities of glycogen phosphorylase (glgP), glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (zwf) and 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (gnd) in the dark, and observed that activity of each enzyme was strongly reduced in the rpaA- strain compared to wild type (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 3C.

claim: The rpaA- strain is unable to activate the carbon catabolic pathways upon the onset of darkness because it cannot induce transcription of the requisite enzymes at dusk
source: Therefore, the rpaA- strain appears to be unable to activate the carbon catabolic pathways upon the onset of darkness because it cannot induce transcription of the requisite enzymes at dusk.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transcriptional and enzymatic activity data.

claim: Glycogen is a crucial metabolic reserve used as a carbon and energy source during periods of darkness
source: Glycogen is a crucial metabolic reserve used as a carbon and energy source during periods of darkness (Smith, 1983).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: In wild type cyanobacteria glycogen accumulates during the afternoon
source: In wild type cyanobacteria glycogen accumulates during the afternoon (Cervený and Nedbal, 2009; Knoop et al., 2010; Rügen et al., 2015) through the activity of a glycogen synthesis pathway composed of phosphoglucomutase (pgm1 and pgm2), ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (glgC) and glycogen synthase (glgA) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior work.

claim: Neither the expression levels nor activity of the glycogen synthesis enzymes are significantly reduced in the rpaA- strain
source: To analyze whether the dawn-arrested rpaA- strain can accumulate glycogen reserves, we measured expression and activity of the glycogen synthesis enzymes and found that neither the expression levels nor activity of the enzymes in the pathway were significantly reduced in the rpaA- strain (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: Glycogen content oscillates over a period of 24 hr in wild type cells both in constant light and in light/dark cycles
source: Surprisingly, we observed that while glycogen content oscillates over a period of 24 hr in wild type cells both in constant light and in light/dark cycles, glycogen is present at a very low level in the rpaA- strain regardless of light conditions, despite high levels of the synthetic enzymes in the extracts (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4D.

claim: Glycogen is present at a very low level in the rpaA- strain regardless of light conditions, despite high levels of the synthetic enzymes in the extracts
source: Surprisingly, we observed that while glycogen content oscillates over a period of 24 hr in wild type cells both in constant light and in light/dark cycles, glycogen is present at a very low level in the rpaA- strain regardless of light conditions, despite high levels of the synthetic enzymes in the extracts (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4D.

claim: The glycogen accumulation defect occurs in the rpaA- 'clock rescue' strain, demonstrating that it is a direct effect of deletion of rpaA
source: The same glycogen accumulation defect occurs in the rpaA- 'clock rescue' strain, demonstrating that it is a direct effect of deletion of rpaA (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4E.

claim: Glycogen synthesis mutants (glgA- and glgC-) exhibit reduced viability in alternating light/dark conditions
source: Like the rpaA- strain, glycogen synthesis mutants (glgA- and glgC-) exhibit reduced viability in alternating light/dark conditions (Gründel et al., 2012), Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, bottom panel) and in constant darkness (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), but grow somewhat slower than the rpaA- strain in constant light conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and 1B with a citation to prior work.

claim: Glycogen synthesis mutants (glgA- and glgC-) exhibit reduced viability in constant darkness
source: Like the rpaA- strain, glycogen synthesis mutants (glgA- and glgC-) exhibit reduced viability in alternating light/dark conditions (Gründel et al., 2012), Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, bottom panel) and in constant darkness (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), but grow somewhat slower than the rpaA- strain in constant light conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Glycogen synthesis mutants (glgA- and glgC-) grow somewhat slower than the rpaA- strain in constant light conditions
source: Like the rpaA- strain, glycogen synthesis mutants (glgA- and glgC-) exhibit reduced viability in alternating light/dark conditions (Gründel et al., 2012), Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, bottom panel) and in constant darkness (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), but grow somewhat slower than the rpaA- strain in constant light conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The deficiency in the preparation of a reserve carbon source may contribute to the impaired viability of the rpaA- strain in the dark
source: We conclude that the deficiency in the preparation of a reserve carbon source – which occurs not at the level of transcription of the glycogen synthesis genes or regulation of the activity of the encoded enzymes – may contribute to the impaired viability of the rpaA- strain in the dark.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the glycogen accumulation data.

claim: Expression of either the missing enzymes or the GalP transporter alone with supplementation of glucose in the rpaA- background is not sufficient to restore viability of this strain
source: Expression of either the missing enzymes or the GalP transporter alone with supplementation of glucose in the rpaA- background was not sufficient to restore viability of this strain (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: Restoration of the carbon utilization pathways combined with the introduction of the glucose transporter in the presence of glucose rescued the viability defect of the rpaA- strain
source: However, restoration of the carbon utilization pathways combined with the introduction of the glucose transporter in the presence of glucose rescued the viability defect of the rpaA- strain (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: Glucose feeding does not increase accumulation of internal carbon stores in the engineered rpaA- strain expressing both the key catabolic enzymes and GalP
source: Glucose feeding does not increase accumulation of internal carbon stores in this engineered strain (Figure 5C), nor in wild type expressing the GalP transporter (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Glucose feeding is sufficient to restore high energy charge in the rpaA- strain expressing both the key catabolic enzymes and GalP
source: However, it is sufficient to restore high energy charge in the rpaA- strain expressing both the key catabolic enzymes and GalP (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and demonstrated in Figure 5D.

claim: Functional circadian output mediated by the activity of RpaA is required for the anticipatory accumulation of carbon reserves during the day
source: Our results strongly suggest that functional circadian output mediated by the activity of RpaA is required for the anticipatory accumulation of carbon reserves during the day, as well as metabolic switching to carbon catabolism at dusk.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Functional circadian output mediated by the activity of RpaA is required for metabolic switching to carbon catabolism at dusk
source: Our results strongly suggest that functional circadian output mediated by the activity of RpaA is required for the anticipatory accumulation of carbon reserves during the day, as well as metabolic switching to carbon catabolism at dusk.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The phosphorylated form of RpaA, regulated by the circadian clock, is critical for the coordination of carbon anabolism and catabolism and cell viability in light/dark cycles
source: Here we show that the phosphorylated form of the transcription factor RpaA, regulated by the circadian clock, is critical for the coordination of carbon anabolism and catabolism and thus cell viability in light/dark cycles.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Deletion of rpaA prevents glycogen accumulation in light
source: Deletion of rpaA prevents glycogen accumulation in light and renders cells unable to utilize existing glycogen at dusk (Figure 5E) – this leads to alterations in cellular energy charge and, as previously observed, to a severe reduction in fitness.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and illustrated in Figure 5E.

claim: Deletion of rpaA renders cells unable to utilize existing glycogen at dusk
source: Deletion of rpaA prevents glycogen accumulation in light and renders cells unable to utilize existing glycogen at dusk (Figure 5E) – this leads to alterations in cellular energy charge and, as previously observed, to a severe reduction in fitness.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and illustrated in Figure 5E.

claim: The inability to accumulate and utilize glycogen in the rpaA- strain leads to alterations in cellular energy charge and a severe reduction in fitness
source: Deletion of rpaA prevents glycogen accumulation in light and renders cells unable to utilize existing glycogen at dusk (Figure 5E) – this leads to alterations in cellular energy charge and, as previously observed, to a severe reduction in fitness.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The mechanism underlying perturbed carbon accumulation in the rpaA- strain is unclear
source: The mechanism underlying perturbed carbon accumulation in the rpaA- strain is unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The activities of glycogen synthesizing enzymes in the rpaA- strain are high in vitro
source: The activities of glycogen synthesizing enzymes in the rpaA- strain are high in vitro, however they could be affected in vivo by the redox state of the cell or by metabolite levels.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by the enzyme activity data in Figure 4C.

claim: Glycogen synthesizing enzymes could be affected in vivo by the redox state of the cell or by metabolite levels
source: The activities of glycogen synthesizing enzymes in the rpaA- strain are high in vitro, however they could be affected in vivo by the redox state of the cell or by metabolite levels.
evidence: This is a speculation about possible mechanisms.

claim: An RpaA-dependent transcript expressed in the afternoon may be required to funnel assimilated carbon into glycogen synthesis
source: It is also possible that an RpaA-dependent transcript expressed in the afternoon is required to funnel assimilated carbon into glycogen synthesis.
evidence: This is a speculation about possible mechanisms.

claim: Additional metabolic flux changes may occur in the rpaA- strain that prevent formation of glycogen stores
source: Alternatively, additional metabolic flux changes may occur in the rpaA- strain that prevent formation of glycogen stores.
evidence: This is a speculation about possible mechanisms.

claim: Anticipation of periodic dark-induced resource limitation is one essential role of the cyanobacterial circadian system
source: Our data support a model in which anticipation of periodic dark-induced resource limitation is one essential role of the cyanobacterial circadian system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The output of the core oscillator, through regulation of RpaA activity, temporally coordinates metabolism to prepare cells for the metabolic demands of periods of darkness
source: The output of the core oscillator, through regulation of RpaA activity, temporally coordinates metabolism to prepare cells for the metabolic demands of periods of darkness.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Correct scheduling of central carbon metabolic activities allows cells to survive the night
source: Correct scheduling of central carbon metabolic activities allows cells to survive the night.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The circadian clock orchestrates a trade-off between rapid cell growth in the morning and robustness to starvation in the afternoon
source: Recently, Lambert et al. observed that the circadian clock orchestrates a trade-off between rapid cell growth in the morning and robustness to starvation in the afternoon, suggesting preparation for the night as a plausible role for the circadian clock (Lambert et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to prior work.

claim: When the periods of the endogenous circadian system and periods of the environmental fluctuations are equal, organisms show a fitness advantage
source: When the periods of the endogenous circadian system and periods of the environmental fluctuations are equal, organisms show a fitness advantage and outcompete mutants whose clocks have an altered periodicity in the same environment (Ouyang et al., 1998; Woelfle et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to prior work.

claim: The fitness defects in the strains with core oscillator periods unequal to the period of environmental variation result from mistiming of RpaA activation
source: Based on our findings, we expect that the fitness defects in the strains with core oscillator periods unequal to the period of environmental variation result from mistiming of RpaA activation.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the findings of the study.

claim: Mistiming of accumulation and mobilization of glycogen stores with the onset of the nightfall would lead to a carbon deficit at night, and impact growth
source: The resultant mistiming of accumulation and mobilization of glycogen stores with the onset of the nightfall would lead to a carbon deficit at night, and impact growth as in the rpaA- mutant during dark periods.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the findings of the study.

claim: One role of the KaiABC clock is to correctly phase the activity of RpaA and downstream carbon metabolism with the external environment, maximizing fitness and growth
source: One role of the KaiABC clock in our model, therefore, is to correctly phase the activity of RpaA and downstream carbon metabolism with the external environment, maximizing fitness and growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and discussion.

claim: Approximately 90 genes have abrogated expression at dusk and throughout darkness in the rpaA- strain
source: Though we show that RpaA activity is crucial for regulation of key aspects of carbohydrate metabolism, we identify ~90 genes whose expression is abrogated at dusk and throughout darkness in the rpaA- strain and it is possible that additional physiological processes are defective in the absence of rpaA.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by the RNA-seq data.

claim: Additional physiological processes may be defective in the absence of rpaA
